extracted.intended_audience: high-school students, coaches, and Art of Problem Solving community members interested in math olympiad competitions
extracted.subtask_description: A brief encyclopedia-style summary of the Chinese Mathematical Olympiad (CMO), giving its purpose, participant composition, problem type, and AoPS difficulty ratings for its problems. Useful for students and coaches seeking quick facts about the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition type
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the contest problems require written proofs rather than multiple-choice or short-answer solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region / scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the national jurisdiction of the contest; the CMO is a Chinese national competition (with guest teams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant composition
rubrics_metrics.description: It features teams from each province of mainland China, along with guest teams from the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau, as well as from Russia and Singapore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who competes — provincial teams plus invited/guest teams — which affects the level and diversity of submissions/solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role in team selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The event plays a key role in selecting the Chinese team for the International Mathematical Olympiad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the contest's importance and that performance here is used as a selection criterion for international representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall difficulty rating
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AoPS difficulty scale for the contest overall; gives a sense of the typical hardness range of problems encountered at the CMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty — Problem 1/4
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AoPS-provided typical difficulty rating for problems in the 1 and 4 positions (useful for anticipating problem hardness and selecting practice problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty — Problem 2/5
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical difficulty rating for problems 2 and 5 on the CMO; indicates moderate-to-high challenge compared with other problem positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty — Problem 3/6
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical difficulty rating for the hardest conventional problems (3 and 6), indicating very challenging problems that often separate top contestants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty — Shortlist / SL 1-2
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical difficulty rating for shortlist problems 1 and 2, indicating easier shortlist items used in selection/training contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty — Shortlist / SL 3-4
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical difficulty rating for shortlist problems 3 and 4, moderate difficulty for shortlist-level practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty — Shortlist / SL5+
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical difficulty rating for shortlist problems 5 and above, covering the hardest shortlist items approaching contest difficulty.
